neet_che_u09_t04_1.working: Cl has the most negative electron gain enthalpy, about -349 kJ/mol. F is only about -328 kJ/mol because of electron repulsion in its compact 2p subshell.

neet_che_u09_t04_2.working: The approximate values are O -141, S -200, Se -195 and Te -190 kJ/mol. O is anomalously low because of its small size, so the order of magnitude is S > Se > Te > O.

neet_che_u09_t04_3.working: Ne has a noble gas configuration and Be has a filled 2s subshell, so both are positive. N has a stable half-filled 2p subshell, so its value is nearly zero or positive.

neet_che_u09_t04_4.working: A is true because adding an electron to O- is opposed by electrostatic repulsion. R is a correct general periodic trend but does not explain A.

neet_che_u09_t04_5.working: Statement I is false because F is less negative than Cl. Statement II is false because the values are swapped: O is about -141 and S is about -200 kJ/mol.
